subject: python
summary: Explains Python file I/O using the with statement, try/except/else/finally execution flow, exception hierarchy best practices, and common encoding pitfalls.
key_points: The with statement automates resource cleanup — files are closed even when exceptions occur.
try/except/else/finally execute in a specific order: else runs only on success, finally runs always.
Catching overly broad exceptions (except Exception) hides bugs and can prevent program termination.
misconceptions: The else block in try/except runs regardless of whether an exception occurred.
except Exception is a safe catch-all that handles errors gracefully.
Omitting the encoding parameter defaults to UTF-8 on all platforms.
check_questions: What resource management problem does the with statement solve?
In what order do try/except/else/finally blocks execute?
Why is TOCTOU a concern when checking file existence before opening?
